messages:
maya: Heads-up — Dedicated canary for eu-west-1 is showing a P90 / P99 jump after yesterday's merge. Notable increase aligned with the prefetch PR (commit a4f3d2c).
jonathan: seeing it too. P95 went from ~45ms -> 120ms on heavy-seq workloads. Any idea which path?
liam: profiler dump looks like KV prefetch misses spiking. The prefetch window alignment change in a4f3d2c seems to shift offsets by one chunk, causing cache shingling.
natalie: can you paste the profiling snippet?
liam: sure — short snippet from nightly perf run:
```
-- before (baseline)
p95: 46ms
p99: 210ms
cache-miss-rate: 6.2%
-- after (canary)
p95: 118ms
p99: 560ms
cache-miss-rate: 24.1%
hot-path: kv_prefetcher::align_window
stack: runtime::get_kv -> prefetcher::align_window -> kernel_selector::choose
```
maya: that's consistent with the SLO alerts. A dedicated customer reported slowdowns for long-context chat flows ~1h ago. SLA risk if this persists.
sre-oncall: Customer-impacting? Which customers/tiers affected?
maya: looks like reserved pools running older kernels but with new prefetch alignment logic applied — dedicated only. Haven't seen hosted API anomalies yet.
jonathan: I ran a local bisect across the prefetcher change set: confirmed regression introduced in a4f3d2c (prefetch window alignment refactor). Repro steps in CI: run perf-bench --profile heavyseq --seq 4096 --batch 8.
liam: CI nightly shows a perf regression flag on the dedicated perf job: https://ci.internal/reports/2008/bench-dedicated. The diff includes an increased miss rate on the KV logs: ``missing_kv_reads++`` spikes.
natalie: options: revert commit, hotfix to restore previous alignment, or throttle prefetcher for dedicated pools. Which has fastest blast radius control?
jonathan: revert is fastest operationally. Hotfix to conditionally preserve old alignment for dedicated would be more surgical but takes a bit longer (30-60m to push + test).
sre-oncall: we need a rollback plan if customer impact grows. Recommend revert on canary and block rollout to prod Dedicated until root cause fixed.
maya: agreed. I'll open a rollback PR and hold current rollout. tagging @deploy-bot to stop the staged rollout.
deploy-bot: action=halt-rollout scope=dedicated-canary user=maya ts=2008459142
jonathan: starting revert PR now: PR #4271 with revert of a4f3d2c. Running unit + perf smoke locally.
liam: also adding a temporary metric to track align_window misses so we can alert earlier.
natalie: ping me when PR passes perf smoke, I'll coordinate with SRE to re-run the canary once reverted.
sre-oncall: please add an incident note if any customers already opened tickets. I'll message CSMs to prep.
maya: logging incident now. Short postmortem to follow after full bisect and root cause analysis.
jonathan: PR merged and deployed to canary at 2008459165. Initial canary metric trend looks promising — p95 back to ~50ms after 2k requests.
liam: still running longer soak, but miss-rate back to ~6.8%. Good sign.
maya: keeping rollout blocked until we get 24h stable canary and CI perf job green. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollout_resume_blocked reason=perf-regression scope=dedicated canary_owner=maya
